sample_unit: patient questions (one response per question per model)

links.outcome: Readability of chatbot responses on rotator cuff surgery in years of schooling
links.effect: Both models showed mean readability corresponding to 13.3 years of schooling (p = 1.000); policy-related questions were the most complex in readability.
links.quote: Both models showed a mean readability corresponding to 13.3 years of schooling ( p  = 1.000).

links.outcome: Editorial reliability of chatbot responses on JAMA benchmark criteria
links.effect: No response met the JAMA benchmark criteria; DISCERN means were 58.7 ± 4.0 (ChatGPT) and 56.3 ± 3.5 (Gemini).
links.quote: No response met the JAMA benchmark criteria.

screen.reason: Empirical evaluation comparing the quality and readability (using DISCERN and readability metrics) of patient-oriented medical information from ChatGPT and Gemini regarding rotator cuff surgery.
